entries.topic: Palantir: origins, US federal footprint, Israel partnership, denials, data purchases

claims.text: Palantir was founded in 2003 by investors including Peter Thiel and took early seed money from In-Q-Tel, the CIA's venture arm; 2019 revenue $746m, nearly half from government; the Army had paid it $135m since a Sept 2018 court ruling

In-Q-Tel's early investment was about $2m; Palantir software deeply embedded at the CIA; relationship with NSA had ended by summer 2015 (Karp: the two sides 'walked away'); pilot work never became a full contract
Snowden documents show Palantir built an 'XKEYSCORE Helper' to move NSA XKEYSCORE data into Palantir; by about 2010 at least three Five Eyes countries used Palantir; Palantir denied link to PRISM
Army enterprise agreement Aug 2025: up to $10bn over 10 years, consolidating 75 contracts (prime on 15, sub on 60)
Maven Smart System: $480m five-year IDIQ May 2024; ceiling raised by $795m to nearly $1.3bn through 2029 (May 2025); more than 20,000 users
FALCON is a customized Gotham for ICE HSI; ICM lets ICE agents access CIA information; 2013 funding doc: Palantir enables real-time info sharing; prior ICM contract worth $41m
ICE's prior Palantir contract was $41m since 2014; 2019 ICM contract about $49m over three years, revealed by a redaction error
2022 ICE award to Palantir of $139.3m for investigative case management operations, maintenance and enhancements

April 2025: ICE to pay Palantir $29.9m for ImmigrationOS; justification: 'Palantir is the only source that can provide the required capabilities'; prototype due 25 Sept 2025; functions: targeting/prioritization, self-deportation tracking, lifecycle tracking
June 2025: ICE preparing a Limiting Sources Justification concluding only Palantir could meet requirements for ICM replacement; replacement deadline Sept 2026

ELITE (reported by 404 Media, Jan 2026) draws on Medicaid and other data, gives a 'confidence score' to addresses; CMS–ICE data-sharing agreement covering nearly 80m Medicaid patients; Palantir/DHS did not comment
19 Feb 2026: DHS blanket purchase agreement with Palantir up to $1bn over five years; CBP, ICE, FEMA, CISA can access
Jan 2024: Palantir held first board meeting of 2024 in Tel Aviv and announced strategic partnership with Israel's MOD to 'supply Palantir technology to help the country's war effort'

Globes 29 Jan 2024: Karp signed upgraded agreement with MOD, photographed with DDR&D head Danny Gold; Palantir understood to work on logistics and manpower, not military intelligence; Unit 8200 and Shin Bet examined it and 'decided not to hire its services'; none of the parties would elaborate
Karp (Mar 2024): 'Israel has historically bought our product, it's not a commercially relevant part of our business'; 'We've lost employees, I'm sure we'll lose employees.'

Palantir to UN Special Rapporteur 22 May 2025: it 'did not provide the technology for, nor is it involved with, Gospel or Lavender'; MOD work 'only began in the wake of the attacks of 7 October 2023'; 'we do not conduct surveillance'
Oct 2024 Storebrand Asset Management sold Palantir holding (~$24m / NOK 262m) citing sales to Israel for use in the occupied territories and predictive-policing systems

Microsoft (25 Sep 2025) disabled an Israeli military unit's use of parts of Azure storage and AI after reviewing Guardian reporting (6 Aug 2025) that Unit 8200 stored recordings of Palestinians' calls; Brad Smith: 'We do not provide technology to facilitate mass surveillance of civilians'
Third-party doctrine: Miller (1976), Smith v. Maryland (1979); Carpenter (2018) refused to extend to historical cell-site data
Chatrie v. United States decided 29 Jun 2026, 6–3: obtaining two hours of Google location records is a search; does not address purchases from brokers
ICE draft memo argued AdID-linked purchased location data differs from Carpenter; CBP–Venntel contracts over $2m 2019–20; ICE 2026 Penlink contract
NSA director Nakasone confirmed to Wyden (published Jan 2024) that NSA buys commercially available netflow data including domestic communications
Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act passed House 17 Apr 2024, 219–199; White House opposed
